headline: Critical cyber threat: AI firm Anthropic warns AI worms may soon reach smart TVs.
body: Anthropic's testers say these AI worms may be months away and hard to switch off. Homes and small firms would likely be hit first; no such attack has happened yet.

headline: Chip maker Nvidia's China AI chip share fell to about a third this year.
body: Research firm IDC estimates Huawei is now close behind Nvidia in China's data centres. Jensen Huang, Nvidia's chief executive, blames US export limits for handing the market to Huawei.

headline: AI firm Anthropic reportedly shows big funds its finances for the first time today.
body: Two unnamed sources say the meeting comes ahead of a possible stock market listing. The figures could show how fast the company grows and whether it profits.

headline: ASML, the Dutch maker of chip-printing machines, cannot fully meet AI demand to 2028.
body: Customers already discuss orders for 2029, says ASML chief executive Christophe Fouquet. If ASML is right, the machines stay scarce and AI services could stay costly.

headline: Oregon's governor halted pollution permits for new data centres until mid-2027.
body: Governor Tina Kotek's letter would pause most large data centre building in the state. Amazon warned of lost jobs, and the pause rests on a letter, not a law.

headline: US safety officials weigh a claim that Tesla's robotaxis speed in school zones.
body: An unnamed petitioner says the driverless cars break speed limits while school zones are active. If true, children near schools are at risk, but nothing has been proven yet.

headline: Digit robot maker Agility Robotics cleared a US step toward a stock market listing.
body: Owners of a listed shell firm will vote on 2 November on merging with Agility. Agility says it would be the only listed US firm solely making working humanoid robots.

headline: Meta launched Muse Wonder, AI models an independent ranking puts near the very top.
body: Ranking group Artificial Analysis puts the larger one second, after AI firm Anthropic's model. Developers can use Muse Wonder now; its safety report and paid app version come later.

headline: Google now lets US adults run apps they made with AI on their Android phones.
body: People describe an app to Google AI Studio, which builds it, then run it privately. The apps stay out of public listings and must still follow Google Play's rules.

headline: China has far more AI researchers than the US and keeps more graduates at home.
body: Scott Singer, an analyst at US think tank the Carnegie Endowment, puts China months behind. Far fewer advanced chips and much less investment hold Chinese AI back.

headline: An OpenAI engineer is charged with hiding a recording device in an executive room.
body: OpenAI says its AI helped find him, and it fired him and alerted the FBI. US officials call it a national security threat; OpenAI sees no sign code was taken.

headline: Johns Hopkins Medicine and AI firm OpenEvidence plan to reshape how doctors train.
body: The plans include AI that weighs fresh evidence with each patient's own history. No dates, costs or results were given, so these are aims, not working tools.

headline: Supermarket chain Kroger will cut 3,000 office jobs as it uses more tech and AI.
body: Kroger's chief executive Greg Foran told staff it must cut work done twice. The cuts run over three years, and no teams or dates have been named yet.

headline: Character.ai, a chatbot app sued over harm to children, has filed for bankruptcy.
body: Character.ai plans a court-supervised sale by year end, and keeps the app running meanwhile. With no good bid, the app closes, leaving over 20 million monthly users without it.

headline: Today's fun fact: a day of OpenAI's always-on AI helper costs about a latte.
body: In security firm Geordie's test, the helper, dot, ran 155 jobs in one day unasked. Hanah-Marie Darley, Geordie's chief AI officer, likens the day's bill to a latte.

headline: Hundreds of scientists asked for a world body to set safety rules for hacking-capable AI.
OpenAI and Anthropic told British lawmakers that AI safety rules should be binding.
Chatbots missed emergencies far more in Vietnamese than in English in a simulated test.
Ex-US vice president Kamala Harris warned that time for AI safety limits is running out.
AI chip shares keep falling as rising interest rates threaten the AI building boom.
body: Chip-machine maker ASML can't fully meet demand, yet chip shares fell on rate fears. Watch TSMC's results on 15 October for demand; not financial advice.
